Chapter 9. Learning to See Ourselves Clearly.
You know, self-justification is something we all do—it’s almost automatic. But here’s the thing: just because it’s natural, doesn’t mean it has to run the show. With a little awareness and practice, you can actually catch your mind in the act, take a breath before jumping to your own defense, and choose honesty... even if it feels a bit uncomfortable at first.
It usually starts with something small. Maybe you feel a spark of defensiveness, a pinch of guilt, or you notice a story you’re telling yourself doesn’t quite fit. Most folks just barrel past these warning signs, eager to feel right again. But if you can pause, even for a second, and ask yourself, “Hey, could I be wrong?”—that’s when real growth begins.
Imagine a parent who snaps at their child after a rough day. The urge to justify it—maybe thinking, “She was being difficult, anyone would have gotten upset”—is so strong. But if that parent takes a moment to reflect, they might realize the outburst was really about their own stress, not the child’s behavior. That honest insight can lead to a real conversation, and before you know it, the relationship gets even stronger.
Or picture a leader who’s made a big mistake. It’s tempting to hide it, blame someone else, or just sweep it under the rug. But when that leader faces up to what happened, learns from it, and tries to make things right, they actually gain more respect and trust from their team.
Seeing yourself clearly isn’t about beating yourself up or feeling ashamed. It’s about being curious, staying humble, and wanting to grow. It means noticing when your mind plays tricks on you—like editing old memories, glossing over your own faults, or hanging on too tightly to beliefs that might not serve you anymore. It also means being open to other perspectives, listening to feedback, and being willing to try something new.
And while this kind of honesty might seem rare, it’s incredibly freeing. You get to drop the exhausting need to be perfect, accept your own humanity, and build deeper, more genuine connections with the people around you.
